newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt Cement shareholders to raise capital.
newsitem.headline: Egypt Cement shareholders to raise capital.

text.p: Egyptian Cement Company (ECC) said on Tuesday it is raising its capital to 390 million pounds ($114.7 million), and a cement plant which it is building in Suez will raise ECC capacity to 2.8 million tonnes in 1999.
An ECC statement said financing for the plant will be raised partially by the capital increase subscribed by shareholders.
ECC is a private-sector firm in which the major shareholder is the local family-dominated group ORASCOM. Swiss cement group Holderbank is also a shareholder.

ECC production capacity will rise to 2.8 million tonnes when the plant comes onstream, from the 1.4 million tonnes it expects to reach at the end of 1998 when ECC's first line, supplied by Krupp's Polysius S.A., starts production in 1998.
Polysius is also constructing the second facility under a contract signed on February 5, bringing total investments for both to about $320 million, the statement said.
Holderbank Financiere Glaris Ltd had previously added 50 million pounds to the ECC capital, raising it to 250 million pounds, an ECC statement had said in October.
